11: That we do not, etc." It is written in Levush that during large meals, people would refrain from eating bread, and even though pieces of bread were left on the table, they did not intend to eat them. This also appears to be the implication in the Tur. However, the Bach wrote that our custom follows the Tosafot, which state that we always intend to eat the bread. Nevertheless, it seems to me (Le'aniyut Da'ati) that the reason is as written in Tosafot Rid, who states: "Specifically in their days, when it was customary to remove the tables before Birkat HaMazon, it appeared as a separate meal. But for us, since we do not remove the table, even if we have finished eating, as long as we have not recited the blessing, it is still considered part of the meal
